Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in liver neoplasm cells, overexpression of PFKFB2 in synergy with canonical glycolytic regulators, namely PGK1 and ZEB1-induced PFKM, intensifies glycolytic activity. This augmented glycolysis yields significant changes in cellular energy and redox states—reflected by increased NADPH and acetyl-CoA levels—that indirectly modulate HMGCR. Such modulation leads to heightened production of geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP), which in turn enhances the geranylgeranylation of proteins. The resultant activation of small GTPases triggers cytoskeletal remodeling and promotes increased cell motility, thereby driving tumor invasiveness and metastasis. To validate this revised cascade, we propose utilizing advanced methodologies including CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene perturbation to modulate PFKFB2 expression, live-cell metabolic imaging and stable isotope-based flux analysis to track glycolytic and intermediate metabolic changes, and high-resolution proteomics combined with live-cell imaging to document protein geranylgeranylation and subsequent cytoskeletal dynamics. This refined hypothesis builds on the original causal chain and integrates contemporary technological capabilities to clarify how metabolic reprogramming is mechanistically linked to liver cancer progression.
Abstract: In liver neoplasms, our refined hypothesis posits that overexpression of PFKFB2, in concert with canonical glycolytic regulators PGK1 and the ZEB1-induced isoform of PFKM, drives an amplified glycolytic flux. This metabolic acceleration generates shifts in cellular energy and redox balances—specifically via altered NADPH and acetyl‐CoA levels and potential AMPK modulation—which subsequently modulate the activity of HMGCR, a key enzyme in the mevalonate pathway. Such modulation leads to increased production of geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP), enhancing protein geranylgeranylation. The post-translational modification activates small GTPases, thereby promoting cytoskeletal reorganization and increased cell motility, ultimately contributing to tumor invasiveness and poor liver neoplasm prognosis. To rigorously test and quantify each step, we propose the integration of state-of-the-art technologies including CRISPR/Cas9 for gene editing, live-cell metabolic imaging, stable isotope-based metabolic flux analysis, and high-resolution proteomics. This multidisciplinary experimental approach aims to elucidate the precise metabolic intermediates linking glycolytic flux to HMGCR modulation and subsequent tumor progression.
CausalChain: PFKFB2 upregulation -> Enhanced glycolytic flux (synergy with PGK1 and ZEB1-induced PFKM) -> Perturbation of cellular energy/redox balance (altered NADPH/acetyl-CoA levels, potential AMPK activation) -> Modulation of HMGCR activity -> Increased geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate production -> Enhanced protein geranylgeranylation -> Activation of small GTPases -> Cytoskeletal reorganization and increased cell motility -> Tumor invasiveness and poor liver neoplasm prognosis
